pages.label: Overview
pages.description: Where AI agents actually get paid today, what the owner must do, and whether it is worth the tokens. Graded shortlist, daily update of edition 3, 24 October 2026: no venue clears every check; under rule v1.2 (published from 22 October), of 27 graded paid venues 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough public data to grade, 17 avoid; nothing moved a grade on 24 October. Correction of 23 October: two TaskMarket deposits we could not find on Base are on Tempo (chain 4217), completed on 22 October; the token is not verified as USDC (grade unchanged). Superteam Earn moves to avoid on 26 October if no agent listing appears (a projection, not a forecast). We list 18 open tasks (paid before is not a promise to pay). About $386.20 reached agent workers on Base in the 30 days to 24 October (estimated, partial). Agent communities pay nothing; 2 of 17 clear our join bar with controls.

pages.label: Where to point your agent this week
pages.description: Graded shortlist, daily update of edition 3, 24 October 2026: no venue clears every check; under rule v1.2, 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough data, 17 avoid. A three-line 'Today' box; a short plain answer led by a correction of 23 October (two TaskMarket deposits are on Tempo, chain 4217, not Base; token not verified as USDC; grade unchanged), TaskMarket's TSK-E49N4V7T unpaid at its grace end (unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid), Superteam Earn's 26 October projection (not a forecast); what changed since edition 3, the 18 open tasks we list with who posted them (paid before is not a promise to pay), the next dates with their checks and a plain table of all 27 venues. The audit trail is one click below.

pages.description: The audit trail behind the plain shortlist top, daily update of 24 October 2026: the TaskMarket deposit check on Base and on chain 4217 with its correction of 23 October and a diagram, TSK-E49N4V7T at its grace end and five tasks paid 53 to 79 days late (a chart), today's feed, counts since edition 3 split by rule, shadow grace record 2 (shadow only, not used for any status) with a labelled sensitivity, odds lines rebuilt, our projections and how they turned out, the full list of 18 open tasks with the chain each names, the daily grade clock to 31 October and beyond (a projection, not a forecast), inputs older than 7 days to 31 October, MoltJobs beside 23 October and an Agent Bounties triage line; below, the 23 October checks with dated correction notes, the edition 3 rule decision and grace, and every earlier dated revision.

pages.label: Is it real? Plain answers
pages.description: Plain answers on whether it pays: is MoltJobs still worth a capped test? (probe first under rule v1.2; its one outside job closed unfunded and unclaimed on 22 October, grade unchanged; its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts), is Algora still paying? (not recently), is TaskMarket real (yes, but small; a correction of 23 October: two deposits are on Tempo, chain 4217, not Base, token not verified as USDC; unpaid at the grace end is a status, not proof it will never be paid), is Superteam Earn legit for agents (partly; winners announced, payment not public), did OpenClaw make money (no, not by itself), does Moltbook still exist (yes; it pays nothing). Each with dated numbers, what we did not verify, and what to try instead, rechecked on 24 October.

pages.label: Getting started
pages.description: Owner checklists for three routes, five checks before any route, the ID, KYC and payout gate per venue, three untested walkthroughs (including Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop), a safety checklist and the calculator at list prices on 11 October 2026 (presets refreshed 12 October, with DeskCrew and MoltJobs presets): attempts and payout per day, whether budget or supply binds, days to first cash and payout per owner hour.

pages.label: Walkthrough: Superteam, owner in the loop
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop: two branches (agent submits and a human claims, or the owner submits the agent's draft), 14 steps with actor, assumed owner minutes, rule rows and KYC, and 6 stop conditions. About one eligible listing every 11 days; payment could not be verified on public routes.

pages.label: Walkthrough: hackbot sign-off
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Ten numbered steps for running a security agent with human sign-off on HackerOne: who acts at each step, the rule row behind it, 8 stop conditions, payout rails and fees, and 5 Bugcrowd differences. Programme policy rows are unverified snippets.

pages.label: Walkthrough: sell per call (x402)
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Eleven numbered steps for selling one narrow service per call over x402: the rules gate against model resale, an owner-held payTo, testnet first, the CDP facilitator, discovery, judging demand by funded wallets, 6 stop conditions and fees. Seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out.

pages.label: Paid opportunities
pages.description: Filterable directory of 27 paid-work and service-selling venues for AI agents, graded by payout evidence and by the shortlist grade with its five checks, who posts the work and what to try instead (grades under rule v1.2, checked 24 October 2026: 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough data, 17 avoid); per-day value, days to first cash, ID and payout gates, owner steps, fees, primary links and dated evidence for each venue. Triage note of 24 October (not graded): Agent Bounties (Base) shows 57 settlements between 14 July and 29 September and none since, largest payout 3 USDC (proposed evidence level E2; owner steps untested; hypotheses labelled).

pages.label: Who actually paid
pages.description: A 30-day ledger of every traced payout to agent workers, on Base only: about $386.20 to 24 October 2026 (estimated and partial, from a fallback route because no address-history route worked for the thirteenth run; 14 new TaskMarket payouts from five tasks paid 53 to 79 days after they expired, from a payer new to the ledger, unlinked, which is not proof of independence). A separate Tempo (chain 4217) line for 10 TaskMarket awards whose token is not verified as USDC. Four escrow balances, TaskMarket's reconciled to the cent. A correction of 23 October: two deposits are on Tempo, not Base.

pages.label: TaskMarket walkthrough
pages.description: How TaskMarket's escrow pays agent workers, and when it does not. 24 October 2026 (rule v1.2): probe first at the low and central bands and avoid at the high band. A correction of 23 October: two deposits we could not find on Base are on Tempo (chain 4217), completed on 22 October; token not verified as USDC. Our grace is 18 days, 15 beside: 1.88% of submissions unpaid at the grace end (3.34% at 15). Five tasks paid 53 to 79 days late (a chart). New: check a TaskMarket deposit yourself, three steps (our reading route; untested as a way to protect an entry).

pages.label: Should your agent join?
pages.description: This week: should your agent join? 17 agent communities re-measured 10 October 2026, OpenClawCity on 11 October: 2 yes with these controls (Moltbook, The Colony), 9 not this week, 6 no; one row per community with the verdict, the controls (untested), the membership cost in tokens at 11 October list prices next to "communities pay nothing", who is active (OpenClawCity 0.64 from its own or templated accounts under our cautious reading, 0.41 as written; none detected on the five re-measured 10 October) and the change since 4 October. The join bar J1 to J7, agent files, light readings, tokens and security.

pages.label: Can my agent do this?
pages.description: Can my agent do this here? Who may submit at each of the 27 graded venues, by the rules text we read, with the deciding rule row linked; 88 rule rows re-read 18 October 2026 (86 re-read, 0 changed; Upwork's legal-page rows re-dated to a 13 October archive copy). A 14-venue × 5-activity grid and a searchable matrix of 207 quoted rule rows, each with its last-read date, and our grading rule v1.2 in plain words. Not legal advice.

pages.label: Spare capacity explained
pages.description: Inference work versus compute rental versus subscription resale, with verified Anthropic, OpenAI (via archive), Google and GitHub Copilot terms, why a paid per-call wrapper around a model is resale, and the two questions no provider answers. Not legal advice.
